title: Your day: separable verbs (Mein Tag)
summary: Describe your day: when you get up, start work, take a break and go home. Meet the separable verbs, whose first part jumps to the end of the sentence.
goals: Describe your daily routine with times
Use separable verbs: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf
Put your day in order with zuerst and dann

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 7: Days and times (Tageszeiten, Emmas Wochenende)

items.de: Eva steht um sieben Uhr auf.

items.en: She has breakfast at half past seven.

items.de: Um neun Uhr fängt die Arbeit an.
Um zwölf Uhr macht sie Pause.
items.en: At twelve she takes a break.

items.de: Am Abend kocht sie und sieht fern.
items.en: In the evening she cooks and watches TV.
At eleven she goes to bed.
items.note: schlafen gehen = to go to bed (literally: go sleeping)

sections.title: Verbs that split
sections.text:
Some verbs have a small first part: [[aufstehen]] is [[auf]] + [[stehen]], [[anrufen]] is [[an]] + [[rufen]], [[einkaufen]] is [[ein]] + [[kaufen]].

In a normal sentence the verb splits. The main part goes to second place as usual, and the small part jumps to the **very end**:
- [[Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.]]
- [[Ich rufe meine Mutter an.]]
- [[Am Samstag kaufe ich ein.]]

Questions work the same way: [[Wann stehst du auf?]] [[Kommst du mit?]]

The small part carries the stress: **AUF**stehen, **AN**rufen. On your word cards the verb appears in one piece, as in a dictionary: [[aufstehen]].

Two of these change their vowel with [[du]] and [[er]]/[[sie]]/[[es]]: [[anfangen]] becomes [[es fängt ... an]], [[fernsehen]] becomes [[er sieht ... fern]]. More verbs like this come in Unit 4.

[[frühstücken]] looks like a two-part verb, but it never splits: [[Ich frühstücke um acht.]]

English does something similar: 'get up', 'pick up', 'call back'. [[Ich hole dich ab.]] = I'll pick you up. The difference: the German small part goes to the very end, after everything else: [[Ich stehe am Montag um sieben Uhr auf.]]

Russian has prefixes too (вставать, позвонить, покупать), but they never leave the verb. In German they do, whenever the verb is in second place.

sections.title: Two ready-made phrases
sections.text: [[Ich rufe dich an.]] = I'll call you. [[Ich hole dich ab.]] = I'll pick you up. [[dich]] is 'you' as the person something happens to. You'll learn this form properly in Unit 4; for now, use these two as they are.

sections.title: First, then: zuerst, dann
sections.text:
To tell your day in order: [[zuerst]] (first), [[dann]] (then). They take position 1, so the verb comes right after them, just as after a time:
- [[Zuerst frühstücke ich, dann arbeite ich.]]
- [[Dann gehe ich nach Hause.]]

[[nach Hause]] = (going) home: [[Um sechs gehe ich nach Hause.]] It's a fixed phrase; Unit 6 explains it. Lesson 5 adds [[zu Hause]], at home.

sections.title: Feierabend
sections.text: [[Feierabend]] is the moment work ends, and the free time after it: [[Um fünf habe ich Feierabend.]] = I finish work at five. When colleagues leave, they say [[Schönen Feierabend!]] = Have a nice evening!

items.en: On Saturday I do the shopping.

items.de: Der Kurs fängt um neun an.
Zuerst frühstücke ich, dann arbeite ich.
items.en: First I have breakfast, then I work.

items.instruction: Fill in the gaps: I get up at seven.
items.explanation: aufstehen splits: stehe in second place, auf at the very end.

items.prompt: On Saturday I do the shopping.
items.explanation: einkaufen: kaufe in second place, ein at the end.

items.question: Which sentence means 'I'm calling my mother'?
items.explanation: anrufen splits, and an goes to the very end, after meine Mutter.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: Are you coming along?
items.explanation: mitkommen: Kommst du mit? The small part goes to the end, in questions too.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: First I have breakfast, then I work.
items.explanation: dann takes position 1, so the verb comes next: dann arbeite ich.
